Nothing behaves wrongly at runtime and no publish verdict is wrong: the guarantee the tab's copy actually makes — "the mouth cannot unbind them" — IS enforced, by the other half of G3 (LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES ⊆ card.tools.locked, compile.py:604-615) and by the live tool grant, which resolves the published card at voice/bot.py:1138-1144 and unions effective_tools (including tools.locked) via agent_core/tools/grant.py:207-213. Every valid card's six values really are "required", so the rendered values are accurate rather than a lie. Dead field + inert tab = MINOR (dead config), not MAJOR.

The four modes are real and default to shadow — reco/config.py:51-62 (RECO_MODE), treatment/config.py:50-64 (TREATMENT_MODE), authority/config.py:23-36 (AUTHORITY_MODE), live_qa/config.py:34-48 (LIVE_QA_BARGE_MODE) — and backend/.env.example ships RECO_MODE=shadow:410, TREATMENT_MODE=shadow:478, AUTHORITY_MODE=shadow:542, LIVE_QA_BARGE_MODE=shadow:555. authority/engine.py:290 is exactly `suppressed = mode != config.MODE_LIVE or matrix.verdict == VERDICT_ESCALATE`. PolicyTab genuinely never reads a mode. Three things are wrong with the finding as filed. (1) The reco citation is off: lines 247-256 are inside the decisions.record(...) features dict; the shadow return (`offers=[], suppressed=True, reason="shadow_mode"`) is at reco/engine.py:270-278. (2) "process-wide: no per-tenant, per-bot or per-card override exists" is false for reco — engine.py:113 resolves `force_mode or arm.mode or config.mode()`, so the Sandbox and the RECO_AB_SPLIT arms both override it per call/per customer. (3) The "lie" framing is over-read: the tab's copy is "These engines decide. The mouth cannot unbind them. ... stay code with a log" (AgentCardPanels.tsx:206-209) — "code with a log" is a literally accurate description of shadow, and the `required` lozenge (226-227) reports the card binding, which really is "required" on every valid card, not an assertion that the engine is live. What survives is a genuine but soft gap: the one screen named Policy gives the operator no read of whether an engine is live, shadow or off. That is MINOR (missing signal), not MAJOR (a lie).

The fact is correct: a Grep for POLICY_KEYS|PolicyKey|POLICY_ENGINES inside AgentCardPanels.tsx returns exactly four lines — the two imports (26, 29) and the local array's declaration and use (55, 211). REQUIRED_POLICY_KEYS and PolicyKey are imported and never referenced; the tab hardcodes its own six-entry list. It compiles because Habibi/tsconfig.json:19-20 sets noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters false. But nothing is incorrect today: the local list matches the shared one exactly (agent-card.ts:116-124 vs schema.py:70-77), and the shared TS constant is itself a hand-maintained copy of the Python tuple, so importing it would not close the drift the finding is worried about — the frontend cannot import schema.py either way. The stated consequence is hypothetical (add a seventh key). Dead imports plus a duplicated literal, with no user-visible defect: TRIVIAL, not MINOR.

The premise holds — G3 fails on `missing_locked` (compile.py:603-615), PATCH /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id} takes an unvalidated `dict[str, Any]` (main.py:2127-2131) and db_prompt_studio.py:1774-1779 writes whatever dict it is handed, and ToolsTab.toggle only rewrites `include` (AgentCardPanels.tsx:103-112) — but the conclusion "permanently blocked with no studio control able to repair it" is wrong, and a guard elsewhere is why. The studio has a first-class Discard Draft control — useDiscardPromptVersion → POST /prompt-versions/{id}/discard (main.py:3365-3368), wired through discardDraft at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:885-926 and the history list at :1569 — which archives that draft and returns the bot to the published card, whose locked list is intact. So the only API-reachable trigger the finding names is repairable in-app in one click. The remaining routes are a hand-edited DB row (not UI- or API-reachable) and "a future template that trims the list" (does not exist: template/scaffold seeds the full four at defaults.py:369, clone copies the source card at clone.py:43-49, and CardTools.locked defaults to LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES at schema.py:114).
